cues.text: Hi Coleman, how are you?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Good thanks.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: I wanted to have a chat with you because our friend Josh told me that you've joined a guitar group and it sounds interesting.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: I'd really like to learn myself.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Why don't you come along? I'm sure there's room for another person.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Really?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: So, who runs the classes?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: He's called a coordinator. His name... Gary Matheson.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Let me note that down. Gary, how do you spell his surname?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: It's M -A -T -H -I -E -S -O -N.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Right, thanks.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: He's retired, actually, but he's a really nice guy and he used to play in a lot of bands.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Thanks. So how long have you been going?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: About a month now.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: And could you play anything before you started?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: I knew a few chords, but that's all.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: I'm sure everyone will be better than me.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: That's what I thought too.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: When I first spoke to Gary on the phone, he said it was a class for beginners, but I was still worried that everyone would be better than me.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: But we were all equally hopeless.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Oh, that's reassuring.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: So, where do you meet?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Well, when I joined the group, they were meeting in Gary's home. But as the group got bigger, he decided to book a room at the college in town.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: I prefer going there.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: I know that place.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: I used to go to tap dancing classes there when I was at secondary school. I haven't been since, though, and I can't remember what road it's in.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Is it Lock Street?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: It's just beyond there, at the bottom of New Street, near the city roundabout.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Yes, of course.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: The guitar club is on the first floor in room T347.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: And when do you meet? Is it at the weekend?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: We meet on Thursdays.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: It used to be 10.30, and that suited me well.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: But now, we meet at 11.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: The class that's in there before us asked if they could have the room for another 30 minutes.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Oh, I see.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Well, I'd love to come, but I don't have a guitar.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Well, you can always buy a secondhand one.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: There's a website called The Perfect Instrument that sells all kinds of guitars, violins, and so on.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: I'm sure you'll find something there.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: So, what's a typical lesson like with Gary?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Well, he always starts by getting us to tune our guitars.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: That takes about five minutes.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Uh-huh.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Some people have an app they use, but others do it by ear.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Gary goes round and helps them.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: And, while he's doing that, he tells us what he's going to do during the lesson.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: First, we usually spend about ten minutes doing some strumming.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: So, is that using...oh, what are they called?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Plectrums?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: No, we just use our thumbs.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Oh, much easier.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Gary reminds us where to put our fingers for each chord, and then we play them together.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Sometimes we all just start laughing, because we're so bad at keeping time.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: So Gary starts clapping to help us.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Do you learn to play any songs?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Yes, we do at least one song with words and chords. I mean, that's harder than you think.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Oh, I'm sure it is.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: That part of the lesson takes about fifteen minutes.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: He often brings a recording of the song, and plays it to us first. Then he hands out the song, and if there's a new chord in it, we practice that before we play it together, but really slowly.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Do you do any finger -picking?
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: That's the last ten minutes of the lesson, when we pick out the individual notes from a tune he's made up.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: It's always quite simple.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: That must be hard, though.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: It is. But people like it, because they can really concentrate.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: And if we're all playing well, it sounds quite impressive.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: The only trouble is that he sometimes gets us to play one at a time.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: You know, alone.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Oh, that's scary.
cues.speaker: Girl

cues.text: Mmm, it is. But I've got used to it now.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: At the end, he spends about five minutes telling us what to practice for the following week.
cues.speaker: Coleman

cues.text: Well, thanks Coleman. I'll go and have a look at that website, I think.
cues.speaker: Girl
